newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES BEAT CARDINALS 5-1, CUBS BEAT GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES BEAT CARDINALS 5-1, CUBS BEAT GIANTS.

text.p: Tom Glavine pitched a seven-hitter for his second complete game of the season and Jeff Blauser's two-run double highlighted a three-run seventh inning as the Atlanta Braves beat the St. Louis Cardinals 5-1 on Sunday.
Glavine (5-2) struck out four and walked two. His only mistake was Ron Gant's seventh homer of the year in the fourth inning.

The Cardinals Andy Benes retired 19 consecutive batters before Javy Lopez singled with two outs in the seventh inning. Mark Lemke followed with a single before Blauser's double gave Atlanta a 3-1 lead.
In Chicago, Sammy Sosa's second home run of the game, a solo shot in the seventh inning, snapped a tie and lifted the Chicago Cubs to a 5-3 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
Sosa belted a 2-0 pitch from Julian Tavarez (0-2) over the centre field fence to give Chicago a 4-3 lead. The Cubs added an insurance run in the seventh on an RBI single by Ryne Sandberg.
"I don't swing at so many bad pitches anymore," Sosa said. "I'm more patient up at the plate, I'm just trying to make contact."

In Cincinnati, Dave Burba and three relievers combined on a nine-hitter and Barry Larkin had a two-run single in the second inning to lead the Cincinnati Reds to a 5-0 victory over the San Diego Padres.
Burba (4-4) scattered seven hits and one walk with five strikeouts in six innings to win for the Reds, who had lost six of their last seven games.
Padres starter Fernando Valenzuela (1-6) allowed three runs -- two earned -- and five hits with three walks and four strikeouts in three innings.
Tony Gwynn went 3-for-4 to raise his average to .377 for San Diego.
In Montreal, Mike Lansing had five hits and drove in three runs, and Pedro Martinez went seven innings to win his seventh game, leading the Montreal Expos to 7-4 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Lansing had two singles, two doubles, a solo homer, a stolen base and scored three runs.
"If I'm getting five hits, I must be contributing some way, so that's always gratifying," Lansing said. "If I get five hits and we lose it doesn't mean as much."
Martinez (7-0) allowed four runs -- three earned -- and six hits, walking one and striking out seven, as his ERA rose to 1.39.

In New York, Rey Ordonez, Manny Alexander and Carl Everett drew bases-loaded walks during an eight-run eighth inning, New York's biggest in more than a year, as the surging Mets defeated the Colorado Rockies, 10-4.
The Mets, who have won 14 of their last 20 games, trailed 4-2 entering the bottom of the eighth inning against reliever Steve Reed.
The Mets tied a club record with 12 walks, a mark they also achieved on Wednesday against Houston.

"I was unable to make adjustments. You start thinking mechanics and I couldn't get back to where I wanted to be," Ruffin said.
"He didn't have a feel at all, he was completely lost out there," Baylor said of Ruffin. "Off the backstop, in the dirt."

In Philadelphia, Garrett Stephenson allowed an unearned run and six hits over seven innings, and Scott Rolen and Darren Daulton hit back-to-back homers in the third inning to lead the Philadelphia Phillies to a 5-3 victory over the Houston Astros.

Stephenson (1-0), making just his second major-league start, struck out four and walked none. He fanned 12 on Tuesday against St. Louis in his first big-league start. Ricky Bottalico pitched the ninth for his 10th save.
"I was spotting my pitches well today, my last game certainly helped me today, I gained a lot of confidence," Stephenson said.

In Pittsburgh, Gregg Zaun and Kurt Abbott delivered RBI singles in the top of the 10th inning as the Florida Marlins won their seventh straight game and completed a three-game sweep of the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-3.
Former Pirate Bobby Bonilla doubled with one out in the 10th against Pittsburgh reliever Rich Loiselle (1-1).
The Marlins overcame a dramatic pinch-hit, two-run homer in the bottom of the ninth by Midre Cummings.
Pittsburgh has lost six of its last eight games.
